subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What default security policy should OpenClaw enforce before externally or plugin-registered recurring agentTurn cron jobs can run on an inherited model?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the fix changes durable scheduling defaults, plugin scheduling contracts, provider/model cost policy, and upgrade behavior, so automation should not choose the boundary.

options.title: Coordinated Cron Safety Policy
options.body: Require operator-visible activation or approval for recurring external/plugin agentTurn jobs and pair it with model-cost visibility plus doctor/update migration guidance.

options.title: Keep enabled-by-default and document operator responsibility
options.body: Treat existing cron.add semantics as the compatibility contract and improve docs/doctor warnings without changing runtime activation behavior.

options.title: Split Into Existing Follow-Ups
options.body: Use the related quota, budget, and provenance issues for separate implementation and keep this issue as the consent/default-model cluster index.

recommendation.title: Coordinated Cron Safety Policy
recommendation.body: Require operator-visible activation or approval for recurring external/plugin agentTurn jobs and pair it with model-cost visibility plus doctor/update migration guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest verified routing evidence is current-main history across cron scheduling, cron model selection, and gateway cron add paths.
